title: Gaussian mean derivative integral bound
statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. For a nonzero variance parameter $v\ge0$ and any $c\in\mathbb R$, \[\left|\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-c}{v}\,p_{c,v}(z)f(z)\,dz\right|\le 1+\frac1v,\] where $p_{c,v}$ is the density of the Gaussian measure with mean $c$ and variance $v$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real number
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. For any function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $|f|\le1$ and any real $c$, $|\int((z-c)/v)p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz|\le1+1/v$, where nonintegrable integrals are assigned zero.
